A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AB-UPT research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and appendix reorganization in v4.

before.justification: v2 reports original surrogate-model experiments on ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML and DrivAerML, including architecture ablations, CAD-based prediction and divergence-free vorticity results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds DrivAerNet++ evaluations, controlled scaling experiments, architectural analyses and additional baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The three-branch architecture, supernode pooling, anchor attention, chunked inference and curl-based vorticity procedure are retained. v4 expands implementation explanations and tests alternative configurations without establishing a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 adds actual evaluation on the geometrically broader, RANS-based DrivAerNet++ dataset, which v2 only discussed. Table 5 also extends the CAD-based prediction scenario from AhmedML to DrivAerML. The original three benchmark datasets remain.

E2.justification: v4 adds comparisons with TripNet's published results and with adapted and published Erwin variants. Table 21 additionally compares the public Transolver++ implementation against Transolver and AB-UPT; v2 reported unsuccessful reimplementation only qualitatively. The main Table 4 comparator set and the existing DoMINO comparison are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled training/inference anchor-count, model-size and training-set-size sweeps, 35-epoch DrivAerNet++ training, and an Erwin comparison using a 700/189 split with 300 epochs and early stopping. The hyperparameter table also revises the reported AhmedML AB-UPT parameter count from 8.75M to 6.7M; this does not establish why the count changed.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's AhmedML design and anchor-versus-interpolation analyses, v4 tests DrivAerML architecture choices, geometry-encoder design, anchor/query training losses, sensitivity to anchor selection and numerical precision. Section 4.8 adds scaling and data-efficiency analyses, while Appendices B.5 and B.7 examine Transolver slices and successive Transolver++ modifications.

E5.justification: The main protocol retains five training seeds, median reporting and averaging over ten evaluation passes. v4 Table 11 newly reports means and standard deviations when query locations are fixed and anchor selections vary for one trained seed. This is a targeted uncertainty assessment, not an established increase in the original repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Existing results are revised: for example, Table 4 changes UPT's DrivAerML vorticity error from 189.6% to 90.2%. Numerous results are added for new benchmarks, analyses and larger model configurations. These are revised or additional findings, not a uniform same-setting performance gain. v4 also contains conflicting GINO vorticity values in Tables 4 and 22, leaving the intended value unresolved.

T1.justification: The governing equations, architecture definitions, anchor-attention complexity analysis, curl construction, finite-difference approximation and normalization derivation are retained. The added explanations and physical limitations do not introduce a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the specific novelty claim for the divergence-free formulation, accompanied by closer attribution to prior constructions in Section 2.3. It also explicitly limits avoidance of CFD meshing to inference. The principal accuracy, scalability, CAD-prediction and physical-consistency contributions remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive limitations concerning simulation fidelity, restricted geometry and flow-condition diversity, and difficulties extending vorticity constraints to mass conservation. New analyses interpret scaling saturation, anchor/query accuracy-cost tradeoffs and possible irreducible noise in DrivAerNet++. Table 1 also replaces the RANS-level accuracy hypothesis with a qualification about comparing simulation fidelities.

D1.justification: v4 adds an inference-code link and important implementation disclosures: relative-coordinate and distance inputs for pooling, precise decoder weight sharing, fp32 positional embeddings and RoPE within mixed-precision training, and PyTorch/CUDA versions. It also explicitly documents concatenating evaluation chunks before calculating metrics and details the additional baseline implementations.

R1.justification: The physical-constraint discussion substantially broadens to distinguish soft penalties, projection-based hard constraints and constraints enforced by construction, explicitly relating AB-UPT to Richter-Powell and Liu. v4 adds connections to neural processes and positioning against Erwin and TripNet, while removing the Lu et al. hard-constraint inverse-design reference.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the abstract, method and conclusion remain intact. v4 makes localized language edits, expands explanations and reorganizes existing appendix material into model-design ablations, extended benchmarks and experimental setup. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v4 adds multi-panel scaling, query-training and baseline-resource plots, structured ablation tables and a streamline comparison. Figure 2 separates surface and volume cell counts, Figure 4 labels physics and decoder blocks, Figure 5 extends the DrivAerML axes, and Table 5 gains DrivAerML columns. Existing DoMINO and reproducibility tables are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation of assumptions that v2 left without dedicated tests, especially inference anchor scaling, query-training discrepancies, geometry-encoder choices and anchor-selection variability. Broader comparisons, implementation disclosures and concrete applicability limitations make the central claims better supported and easier to assess. Numerical inconsistencies remain between main and appendix tables, but they do not outweigh these substantial gains in validation and transparency.
